question: Will New York City rent grow above 4% in December 2026?

profile.label: Adults 25+ with a bachelor's degree or higher

questions.text: Will rent in New York City be more than 4% higher in December 2026 than in December 2025, according to the StreetEasy Rent Index (all bedrooms)?
How did your rent change the last time your lease renewed?

answers.option: It went up by less than 3%
It went up by more than 6%
I haven't renewed a lease yet

behaviorSummary: 60% say their last renewal raised rent by 3% or more (38% by 3% to 6%, 22% by more than 6%). 20% saw a rise under 3%, 19% saw rent stay the same or go down, and 1% have not renewed yet.

quotes.text: My rent already jumped 8% last renewal because the landlord said it was to match nearby listings, so I don't see NYC slowing down enough to stay under 4% by next December.
My last renewal went up 7%, and with how tight the rental market still feels in Brooklyn, I don't think prices will cool off enough to stay under a 4% increase by then.
My last renewal went up 5%, and with insurance, maintenance, and everything else climbing, I don't see NYC rents easing enough to stay under 4% by December 2026.
I don't expect rents to rise much more than that because my own regulated renewal was only a small increase, and with tenants already stretched, I think the market will stay fairly restrained.
Inventory feels more balanced and landlords are already giving concessions, so I don't see rents accelerating enough to clear 4%.

knownAnswerCheck.question: Was rent in New York City more than 4% higher in October 2026 than in October 2025, according to the StreetEasy Rent Index (all bedrooms)?
knownAnswerCheck.fact: The StreetEasy Rent Index for New York City was $4,014 in October 2026 and $3,793 in October 2025, a rise of 5.8%, which is more than 4%.
knownAnswerCheck.sourceName: StreetEasy Rent Index, New York City, all bedrooms (StreetEasy data dashboard)
